Graham Hancock and Randall Carlson appear together on episode 1897 of the Joe Rogan Experience, a pairing fans of ancient mysteries treat as a main event. Hancock argues a lost ice-age civilization taught the ancient world. Carlson, a geologist by training, backs the catastrophe side of the case.

Together they lay out their evidence: flood myths, old monuments, and signs of a comet strike near the end of the last ice age. Rogan referees and marvels by turns. The episode is the duo's fullest joint statement on the show, a long, detailed brief for a past far stranger than the textbooks allow.

Comedian Joe DeRosa returns to Joe Rogan for episode 2538. DeRosa is a regular in Rogan's circle of comics. His humor runs dark, dry, and self-aware.

The pair trade stories from clubs, tours, and years on the road. DeRosa shares his takes on food, fandom, and the grind of stand-up. Rogan knows his act well, so the talk stays loose. Fans of either man get the feel of two old friends recording the chat they would have had anyway, microphones or not. Their ease marks years of shared rooms and roads.
